key_insight: Accurate PDE predictions do not guarantee accurate responses to small input changes. TangentPDE adds sparse finite-difference supervision to help neural operators learn these local responses.
problem_solved: Training mainly on state reconstruction constrains predictions at observed inputs but can leave a neural operator’s sensitivity to nearby perturbations poorly learned.
method: Approximate directional derivatives using finite differences between perturbed inputs.
Use sparse finite-difference supervision to constrain local operator responses.
Focus on task-relevant perturbation directions alongside accurate state prediction.
impact: Learning local responses could make neural PDE operators more useful in sensitivity-aware tasks, such as optimization and control. The supplied abstract is incomplete, so experimental gains and application results cannot be assessed.
visual_elements: Side-by-side illustration: matching a state value versus matching both the value and local slope.
Perturbation diagram showing an input, a nearby input, and the corresponding change in PDE output.
Training schematic linking state prediction and finite-difference supervision to a neural operator.
Conceptual response curves showing how models with similar state predictions can have different local sensitivities.
paper_title: TangentPDE: Learning Local Operator Responses with Sparse Finite-Difference Supervision
paper_authors: Xinjian Xie, Ruxuan Chen, Jiashu Li, Tianyu Gao, Ye Wei
